name: Oklahoma
overview: In Oklahoma, each county treasurer sells real estate with long-delinquent property taxes at an annual resale, which state law sets for the second Monday of June in every county. The real estate is sold at public auction to the highest bidder for cash or certified funds, and the treasurer may choose to hold the June resale as an online auction. Property bid off in the county's name is deeded by the county treasurer to the board of county commissioners. Owners who redeem delinquent taxes pay interest at the lawful rate set in Section 2913 of the tax code; minors and incapacitated persons may redeem within one year after their disability ends, with interest and penalty capped at ten percent a year.

counties.how_to_bid: Pre-registration is encouraged at the Treasurer's office beginning approximately May 15th; once the sale begins, registration is only accepted at the auction location. A pre-deposit of $500.00 or more is recommended. Cash, cashier's check or money order is accepted, and buyers without a pre-deposit pay immediately after each purchase. The minimum bid is the lesser of 2/3 of the current tax year assessed value or the advertised taxes, interest, fees and costs. Properties not sold go to the county and may later be sold by auction with Board of County Commissioners approval.

counties.how_to_bid: Based on the Treasurer's 2026 bidder packet: bid online through GovEase; registration opens about two weeks before the sale, and anyone bidding for a company must register as a bidder for that company. The deposit is 10% of the amount you want to be approved to bid. Winners pay the online vendor by 4:30 pm CST the following day; the Treasurer's office does not accept funds in person for this. A 5% bidder's premium and a $10 deed fee are added. Successful bidders receive a Treasurer's Resale Deed issued within a week of the June Resale.

counties.how_to_bid: County-owned property (acquired at annual delinquent-tax sales) is sold by Commissioner's Sale: the bidder completes and signs a bid sheet; if the County Commissioners approve the starting bid, the Treasurer's office sets the date of sale. A deposit of the starting bid amount plus a minimum of $187.00 (estimated publication costs and fees) is required in certified funds. The sale ad runs for three consecutive Wednesdays before the sale. All bidders must be registered by 8:45 a.m. in the Treasurer's office on sale day and be present. Costs and fees are charged to the highest bidder; on Commissioners' approval the Treasurer issues a deed to the highest bidder. Each deed holder must sign a notarized Affidavit of Land or Mineral Ownership; buyers research liens themselves.

counties.how_to_bid: The June resale is an open, active auction at the Treasurer's office (Mayes County Courthouse, 1 Court Place, Ste 100, Pryor) where property is sold to the highest bidder. You or your representative must be present; to get a bidder number you give your name, address and telephone number on the sign-in sheet. The minimum bid is the delinquent amount due or two-thirds of assessed value, whichever is less. All payments must be cash (no checks or credit cards); buyers also pay a $10 deed fee and about $20 for recording. The owner may redeem any time before the deed is executed. No deposit or registration deadline stated.
